title: San Francisco: New York Man Sentenced for $7M Cryptocurrency Scam Tied to Silicon Valley Investors - NewsBreak
text: SAN FRANCISCO – A New York man who spent several years in the Bay Area was sentenced to four years in federal prison after defrauding investors of more than $7 million in cryptocurrency and other funds, according to a Department of Justice statement released Friday. Douglas Jae Woo Kim, 32, was convicted by a federal jury in February 2025 on 14 counts, including wire fraud and money laundering, following a three-week trial in San Francisco. Senior U.S. District Judge Charles R. Breyer handed down the 48-month sentence during a hearing held in San Francisco, where Kim had lived while conducting the scheme. At sentencing, Judge Breyer dismissed one of the money laundering counts on jurisdictional grounds, the Department of Justice reported. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Kim operated the fraudulent investment scheme from October 2017 to June 2020 after relocating to San Francisco. Prosecutors said Kim targeted individuals in the area—many of whom were friends or acquaintances—by claiming to be a legitimate cryptocurrency trader. The Justice Department said Kim promised high returns on what he described as short-term, low-risk loans and assured victims their investments were personally guaranteed. In one case that began in October 2017, Kim contacted a victim via text, claiming he was seeking investors for a “fairly modest operation.” Kim told the victim the venture involved cryptocurrency profits from peer-to-peer network fees and exchanges and that it “isn’t very risky to me,” according to court testimony cited by prosecutors. Over time, the victim sent more than $1 million to Kim, most of which prosecutors said ended up on offshore sports betting sites. Another victim was approached by Kim in November 2017 via email. Kim claimed he needed cryptocurrency for a trading strategy and reassured the victim that “my activities are fairly low risk.” This person ultimately lost over $500,000, according to the Department of Justice, with much of that money also sent to offshore gambling platforms. A third victim, prosecutors said, entered into an investment agreement with Kim on January 1, 2018. The arrangement involved approximately $200,000 worth of cryptocurrency, which Kim quickly converted to bitcoin and transferred to an offshore casino. That victim lost more than $4 million overall, the Justice Department said.
